title: Adaptive Simulation Run Record
description: Schema for one line of an adaptive-simulation provenance log (JSONL). Each record is a complete, replayable account of a single simulation run: the parameters it used, the seed it ran under, what it produced, which claims held, and the reasoning that led to the next run.

run_id.description: Stable identifier for this run. Derived from model, iteration and seed so the same experiment yields the same id.

model_name.description: Registered model this run executed (e.g. forest, fluctuating).

parameters.description: Full parameter set handed to the model. Must be JSON-native so the run can be replayed from the log alone.

random_seed.description: Seed of the RNG stream this run consumed. Replaying with this seed and these parameters reproduces the outcomes.

timestamp.description: Unix time at which the record was written.

duration_seconds.description: Wall-clock cost of the run. Non-negative — time does not run backwards (IRREVERSIBILITY).

outcomes.description: Measured results of the run. Model-specific; keys are whatever the model reports.

claim_results.description: Verdict per claim tested against this run's outcomes.

reasoning_chain.description: Ordered reasoning steps the agent took after observing this run. Empty only if nothing was recorded.

experiment.title: Discrepancy Arm
experiment.description: Present when the run is one arm of a discrepancy sweep — a fork in the model's specification that was resolved by experiment rather than by assertion. Absent for ordinary adaptive-loop runs.

discrepancy_id.description: Which open question this run is evidence about.

option_label.description: Which reading of the question this run took.

option_index.description: Position of the option in the discrepancy's option list.

reasoning_step.title: Reasoning Step
reasoning_step.description: One observation -> hypothesis -> action link in the chain. Keeps provenance intact: every parameter change points back at the observation that motivated it.

hypothesis.description: Why the agent thinks the observation looks the way it does.

action.description: What the agent changed in response.

expected_outcome.description: What the agent expects the next run to show if the hypothesis holds. Written before the next run — this is what makes the step falsifiable.

parent_step_id.description: Step this one descends from, or null at the root of a chain.
